# Book of Giants Fragment 12 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 4Q532 frag. 2 (Cave 4) | **Condition:** extremely fragmentary; only isolated words and phrases survive

---

**12:1** [...] in-the-days-of [...] the-word-of [...] the-judgment-of God [...]

**12:2** [...] came upon all the-inhabitants-of the-earth [...]

**12:3** [...] for-the-wickedness was-great [...]

**12:4** [...] and-the-corruption was-complete [...]

**12:5** [...] and-all the-earth was-filled with-violence [...]

**12:6** [...] and-all flesh [...] was-destroyed [...] except [...]

**12:7** [...] those-whom God preserved [...]

**12:8** [...] according-to-His-mercy [...]

**12:9** [...] and-the-righteous-ones [...] were-saved [...]

**12:10** [...] from-the-destruction [...]

**12:11** [...] and-the-earth [...] was-purified [...] from [...] corruption [...]

**12:12** [...] and-from-all the-defilement [...]

**12:13** [...] which the-Watchers and-their-sons had-brought upon-it [...]

**12:14** [...] and-the-earth was-renewed [...]

**12:15** [...] and-righteousness grew-up upon-it [...]

---

*EMET notes: Fragment 12 (Final Fragments). Source: 4Q532 frag. 2. Aramaic text from Cave 4 Qumran. Hyphenated compounds preserve Aramaic construct-chain syntax and bound morphemes. Square brackets indicate genuine manuscript lacunae where the leather has deteriorated or broken away. The Book of Giants is an Aramaic expansion of the Watcher myth from 1 Enoch 6-16, featuring the Nephilim giants Ohya, Hahya (sons of Shemihazah), Mahaway (son of Baraq'el), and the hero Gilgamesh.*
